notes:
Written by ea-07 on 2026-10-25 from four pages (budget 2-5; the Haixi page is thin). The Haixi (Hulun) Jurchens are a tribal state Cliopatria lacks: the three keyframes are new and no Cliopatria shape is reviewed.

Drawn from the pages: the dates (1520s appearance, 1548 Wang Tai, 1582 his death, 1601 Hada, 1607 Hoifa, 1613 Ula, 1619 Yehe) and 'based primarily in modern Jilin province'. Read, not drawn by a page: every shape. The Hada disc at Tieling stands for the Guangshun Pass trade country east of Kaiyuan (Kaiyuan is not in the gazetteer); the Jilin disc (130 km) and the Siping disc (70 km) for the Ula and Hoifa and the Yehe are the same stand-ins that later-jin-dynasty uses, with no place on any page I opened. The Haixi page's 'parts of modern-day Jilin, Heilongjiang, Liaoning, and Inner Mongolia' is far wider and is not drawn.

Disagreements and gaps: the Hada fall in 1601 (Haixi, Hulun and unification pages) or 1603 (Nurhaci page); whether the Haixi confederacy dates from the 1520s or from Wang Tai in 1548; the Ming vassalage ('accepted vassal status', Manchuria under Ming rule, undated; Hada leaders' Ming titles 'as of 1599') is not in the ming-dynasty ledger, since no page gives a year for the relation; the Wild Jurchens (defeated in 1611) and the Nurgan tribes have no dossier. The state has no capital (the pages name no seat other than 'the seat of Haixi Chieftain Gintaisi' in 1619). Rulers: Wang Tai (Hada, 1548-1582) and Gintaisi (Yehe, to 1619) are named by the pages but no list gives the other years.

Counterparts: 'jianzhou-jurchens' for 1601-1613 (Nurhaci's polity before the Jin), 'later-jin-dynasty' for the 1619 end.
